title: k-NN Classify
statement: Implement `knn_predict(train_x, train_y, query, k)`. Distance is Euclidean. Break distance ties by the smaller training index so the result is deterministic. Among the k nearest labels, return the majority label. If votes tie, return the smaller label.
constraints: Every training row has the same dimension as query

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.explanation: Exact k-NN scans the training set. Ball trees and HNSW approximate this when n is large.

editorial: k-NN memorizes the training set and predicts by local vote. Sorting by (distance, index) makes equal distances deterministic: the earlier training row wins. Vote ties break toward the smaller label so tests do not depend on dict ordering. Choose odd k for binary problems when you want to avoid ties, scale features before measuring distance, and remember that prediction cost grows with the training set unless you add an index.
